identity.name: Protectorate General to Pacify the South
identity.wikipedia: Protectorate General to Pacify the South

land.text: 'In 679, the Annan Protectorate replaced the Jiaozhou Protectorate' (also called Jiaozhi), 'located in modern-day Vietnam'; Jiaozhou had covered parts of modern Guangdong, Guangxi and northern Vietnam

predecessors.note: The Jiaozhou Protectorate was a Tang unit, not a separate state; the Third Era of Northern Domination lasts to 938.

land.text: 'Gao Pian ... recaptured Songping, the capital of Annan' and 'renamed the region of Annan to Jinghai Jun' after 866

capitals.name: Songping (Tống Bình, Hanoi)
capitals.note: 'Situated in Songping County' in present-day Hanoi; Nanzhao held it 863-866.

correction.text: the Annan Protectorate: northern Vietnam from the Red River delta south through Thanh Hoa and Nghe An to Ha Tinh, seat at Songping (Hanoi)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The page says only that the protectorate was 'located in modern-day Vietnam' with its seat at Songping, and that revolts rose in Hà Tĩnh (722) and around Songping; Nanzhao held the capital 863-866 (occupation event, drawn hatched, not a change of shape). Tonkin plus Thanh Hóa, Nghệ An and Hà Tĩnh is the researcher's reading, probably over-wide at the south and inland. No area figure on the page. Area check: no infobox figure; the whole reading (Tonkin, Thanh Hoa, Nghe An, Ha Tinh, about 134,000 km2) is about 2.2 times Cliopatria's Ngô Dynasty shape of 947 (62,155 km2), so it is probably over-wide at the south and inland. Split in the repair: 679-802 whole, 803-808 without Nghe An and Ha Tinh (seized by Huanwang), 809-866 whole again.

correction.text: the Annan Protectorate without southern Annan (Nghe An and Ha Tinh), seized by the Cham state of Huanwang in 803 and recovered in 809

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'In 803, a northern state of Champa, Huanwang, seized southern Annan' (protectorate page). The page does not name the provinces; Nghe An and Ha Tinh are the reading the champa and tang-dynasty dossiers use for the same event (803 gain / 803 loss). The Champa page has 'the Chinese barely defeated the Cham and recovered lost regions in 809'; the protectorate page does not mention the recovery.

correction.text: the Annan Protectorate: northern Vietnam from the Red River delta south through Thanh Hoa and Nghe An to Ha Tinh, seat at Songping (Hanoi)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The same extent as 679-802 after 'the Chinese barely defeated the Cham and recovered lost regions in 809' (Champa page); the protectorate page lists Zhang Zhou (806-810) and Ma Zong (810-813) as protector-generals but does not connect them to a reconquest. Nanzhao's occupation of Songping 863-866 is an occupation event, not a change of shape.

region.text: the Annan Protectorate: northern Vietnam from the Red River delta south through Thanh Hoa and Nghe An to Ha Tinh, seat at Songping (Hanoi)

ledger.note: 679: the Annan Protectorate replaces the Jiaozhou Protectorate. 'In 679, the Annan Protectorate replaced the Jiaozhou Protectorate'; the seat is Songping (Hanoi).

region.text: Annan, held by the rebels until the Tang retook it in 791

ledger.note: 785: Phung Hung's revolt. 'Do Anh Han, Phung Hung and Phung An rebelled against doubled taxes'; 'Tang forces retook Annan in 791'. The page does not say which parts the rebels held, so the whole protectorate is the zone.
791: the Tang retake Annan. 'Tang forces retook Annan in 791' from the rebels of Do Anh Han and Phung Hung.

region.text: southern Annan, seized by Huanwang (Nghe An and Ha Tinh are the researcher's reading, as in the champa dossier)

ledger.note: 803: Huanwang seizes southern Annan. 'In 803, a northern state of Champa, Huanwang, seized southern Annan.' The page names no province; Nghe An and Ha Tinh follow the champa dossier (803 gain) and the tang-dynasty dossier (803 loss). The page adds that 'from 803 to 863, local rebels killed or expelled no fewer than six protector-generals of Annan'.

region.text: the regions lost in 803 (Nghe An and Ha Tinh)

ledger.note: 809: the Chinese recover southern Annan. 'The Chinese barely defeated the Cham and recovered lost regions in 809' (Champa page); mirror of champa 809 and tang-dynasty 809. The protectorate page does not mention the recovery.

863: Nanzhao takes Songping. 'In mid-January Nanzhao returned with about 50,000 troops and besieged Songping'; on 28 February Yang Sijin entered the inner city and Cai Xi drowned. Nanzhao also besieged Junzhou (Haiphong) from 20 June. Mirror of nanzhao's 863 occupation.
866: Gao Pian retakes Annan. 'Gao completed the retaking of Annan' in the autumn of 866 and executed the Nanzhao general Duan Qiuqian.
866: Annan becomes the Jinghai Circuit. Gao Pian 'recaptured Songping, the capital of Annan' and 'renamed the region of Annan to Jinghai Jun'; the protectorate's span ends 866.

wars.name: Liu Yanyou's tax revolt (Lý Tự Tiên and Đinh Kiến)
belligerents: Lý Tự Tiên and Đinh Kiến rebels
wars.outcome: Liu Yanyou's attempt to levy full taxes on the Li people sparked a revolt that took Songping; Cao Xuanjing put it down.
wars.note: No land changes hands for the ledger; the page gives no month or length.

wars.name: Revolt of Mai Thúc Loan

zones.text: Hà Tĩnh province, where Mai Thúc Loan rebelled

wars.outcome: Mai Thúc Loan rebelled in what is now Hà Tĩnh in 722 and was defeated in 723.
wars.note: The page does not say whether the rebels held ground beyond Hà Tĩnh.

wars.name: Revolt of Phùng Hưng

zones.text: the Annan Protectorate: northern Vietnam from the Red River delta south through Thanh Hoa and Nghe An to Ha Tinh, seat at Songping (Hanoi)

wars.outcome: Do Anh Han, Phung Hung and Phung An rebelled against doubled taxes in 785 and the Tang retook Annan in 791.
wars.note: The page says 785; some accounts say 782.

wars.name: Huanwang (Champa) seizure of southern Annan

zones.text: southern Annan (Nghe An and Ha Tinh)

wars.outcome: A northern Cham state, Huanwang, seized southern Annan in 803 and 'the Chinese barely defeated the Cham and recovered lost regions in 809'.
wars.note: The protectorate page gives 803 only; the 809 recovery is on the Champa page.

wars.name: Tang-Nanzhao conflicts in Annan
wars.outcome: Nanzhao raided from 846 and 858, briefly took Songping on 17 January 861 (retaken 21 July), took it again on 28 February 863 and held it until Gao Pian retook Annan in autumn 866.
wars.note: The 861 interlude is too short for a yearly occupation event.

certainty.note: No frontier is drawn on either page; the southern and western limits are the researcher's reading.

sources.title: Protectorate General to Pacify the South
sources.note: 679 founding, Songping seat, the revolts of 687, 722 and 785, Nanzhao 863, Gao Pian 866, the Jinghai renaming.

sources.title: Tang-Nanzhao conflicts in Annan
sources.note: The 861 fall and retaking of Songping, the 863 siege and fall (28 February), Gao Pian's 866 retaking.

sources.title: Champa
sources.note: Re-read for the repair: 'The Cham assaulted the Tang and seized Nghe An in 803'; Huanwang, a northern Cham state, invaded Annan in 803; 'The Chinese barely defeated the Cham and recovered lost regions in 809'.

sources.title: Phung Hung
sources.note: Opened for the 785-791 rebel extent: the page names Duong Lam as his home and says he 'laid siege to the headquarters of the Annam Protectorate' and ruled 11 years; it gives no territory, so the whole protectorate stays the contest zone.

notes: Written for ea-04-x on the Andong protectorate's pattern (type colony). The Tang dossier carries the same land: a 863 loss and 866 gain with nanzhao as loss/gain events, where this dossier and nanzhao use occupation events. Repair (2026-10-19, after review): the first version said no page mentioned the 803 loss to Champa; the protectorate page does ('In 803, a northern state of Champa, Huanwang, seized southern Annan'). The 803 loss and 809 gain (counterpart champa, region Nghe An and Ha Tinh as in the champa and tang-dynasty dossiers, confidence 2) are now in the ledger, the keyframe is split at 803 and 809, and the war is listed. The protectorate page does not mention the 809 recovery, which is on the Champa page. The Phung Hung rebels (785-791) held Annan on the page's wording ('retook Annan in 791'); the Phung Hung page opened in the repair gives no territory, so the contest zone stays the whole protectorate (confidence 2) and the rebels have no dossier; the other counterparts in wars are names only. Tonkin plus Thanh Hoa, Nghe An and Ha Tinh is a reading; the Tonkin region of the gazetteer ends at the Ninh Binh-Thanh Hoa line, and the shape is about 2.2 times Cliopatria's Ngô 947 shape (62,155 km2).
